episode.title: Allow a keyless cloud-provider configuration to resolve Application Default Credentials without changing principals
episode.before: At parent c2d63fbe582a3d37051816dea4775687a4ab9896, both CLI authentication validation and core model validation required an API key for the vertex-ai authentication type. Supplying a placeholder key passed those gates but caused the SDK to select Express authentication instead of the configured project and Application Default Credentials. Client construction relied on an optional vertexai field or an environment-variable side effect, and ACP preflight treated the absence of registered key variables as a warning rather than distinguishing project routing configuration from a resolved credential.
episode.after: At fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430, a shared nonblank-project predicate permits the Application Default Credentials path only for the vertex-ai authentication type when no provider-specific key variable is declared. CLI and core validators accept that keyless configuration, retain declared key variables as authoritative, and give the project-based alternative only where it can work. Client construction derives Vertex mode directly from the selected authentication type while leaving the API key absent for SDK credential resolution. ACP preflight reports the project-only configuration as indeterminate rather than claiming that a token exists.
episode.diff: The commit modified 12 files with 384 insertions and 14 deletions. It added a shared project-configuration predicate; added ADC eligibility checks to CLI and core credential gates; preserved explicit provider key requirements; derived SDK Vertex mode from authentication type; added conditional missing-credential guidance; changed ACP project-only preflight reporting to unknown; documented the keyless path; and added CLI, core, client-construction, and ACP tests covering successful project-only validation, missing-project failures, whitespace rejection, provider-specific key precedence, authentication-type isolation, absent API-key propagation, and indeterminate preflight status.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430 has parent c2d63fbe582a3d37051816dea4775687a4ab9896, resolves issue 9016 through PR 9017, and states that mandatory API-key validation prevented ADC or service-account startup while placeholder keys selected Express mode.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0] and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: The parent core validator required an API key for every non-OAuth authentication type and emitted a missing-key error whenever config.apiKey was absent.

The new core implementation defines a shared predicate that accepts only a nonblank GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and recognizes ADC only when the authentication type is vertex-ai, no apiKeyEnvKey is declared, and the project predicate succeeds.

Core model validation changed from unconditional missing-key rejection to rejection only when neither an API key nor an eligible project-based ADC configuration is present; the declared apiKeyEnvKey is also passed into error construction.

CLI validation resolves the selected provider entry, excludes entries declaring envKey from ADC fallback, reads project configuration from process environment or settings.env through the shared predicate, and accepts a keyless project only when the entry is ADC-eligible.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/cli/src/config/auth.ts, isVertexAdcEligible, hasVertexProject, and validateAuthMethod

evidence_units.claim: CLI tests accept project-only configurations from both process environment and settings.env, reject configurations with neither key nor project, reject whitespace-only projects, and continue requiring a provider entry's declared key variable even when a project exists.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/cli/src/config/auth.test.ts, validateAuthMethod Vertex AI test cases

evidence_units.claim: Client construction now derives vertexai=true from the selected vertex-ai authentication type when no explicit vertexai value is supplied, and converts an empty API key to undefined so the SDK can resolve its non-key credential path.

Core tests prove that project-only vertex-ai validation succeeds in normal and strict modes and that client construction invokes GoogleGenAI with vertexai=true and apiKey=undefined even when the mode environment-variable side effect is unset.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts, validateModelConfig - Vertex AI Application Default Credentials

evidence_units.claim: Core tests also prove that a missing project remains invalid, the keyless path is not extended to the Gemini API authentication type, and an explicit apiKeyEnvKey remains mandatory without project-based advice.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.test.ts, negative and explicit-key Vertex ADC cases

evidence_units.claim: Resolved model configurations pass through validateModelConfig before generator creation, and both Gemini API and vertex-ai authentication types are routed to createGeminiContentGenerator.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/core/src/core/contentGenerator.ts lines around createContentGeneratorConfig and createContentGenerator

evidence_units.claim: Missing-credential errors append a shared project-based ADC hint only for vertex-ai configurations without an explicit provider key variable.

CLI and core tests require missing-credential messages for eligible vertex-ai configurations to mention GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT while suppressing that advice for other authentication types and entries with declared key variables.

ACP preflight detects a keyless vertex-ai configuration with a nonblank project and reports status and hasToken as unknown, explicitly treating project selection as routing configuration rather than proof of a resolved credential.
The ACP test invokes workspacePreflight for a project-only vertex-ai setup and verifies unknown status, unknown hasToken, and no errorKind.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.test.ts, keyless Vertex preflight test

evidence_units.claim: The workspacePreflight extension method calls buildAcpPreflightCells, which includes the modified authentication preflight cell.
evidence_units.source: git show fd9c452dc889d27338ab1e2e9a2b22aebcfc5430:packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts, workspacePreflight dispatch and buildAuthPreflightCell

evidence_units.claim: Documentation states that project-only authentication requires explicit selection of the vertex-ai authentication type, requires envKey and every other API-key source to remain unset, and does not permit an entry with declared envKey to fall back to ADC.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-project-based-credential-eligibility
candidate_atomics.description: Classify a project-only configuration as eligible for default credential resolution only when the selected authentication mechanism supports it, the project identifier is nonblank, and the provider entry has not declared a mandatory key variable.

semantic_action.intent: Permit the supported keyless credential path without silently replacing an explicitly configured credential principal.
semantic_action.module_role: credential eligibility policy shared by configuration gates
semantic_action.pre_state: Credential validation sees no resolved API key and previously treats that absence as invalid regardless of project routing configuration.
semantic_action.post_state: A project-only configuration is eligible precisely when its authentication type supports default credentials, its project value is nonblank, and no provider-specific key variable is declared; all other missing-key configurations remain invalid.
semantic_action.validation: CLI and core unit tests cover process and settings project sources, whitespace rejection, authentication-type isolation, and precedence of a declared key variable.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-credential-validation-gates
candidate_atomics.description: Apply the same credential eligibility rule at both early CLI validation and core session/model validation so a valid keyless configuration is not rejected by either gate.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a supported default-credential session to pass every startup validation boundary consistently.
semantic_action.pre_state: Early CLI and core validators independently require an API key, blocking project-based default credentials before client startup.
semantic_action.post_state: Both validation boundaries accept the same eligible project-only configuration while retaining missing-credential failures for ineligible configurations.
semantic_action.validation: CLI tests assert null validation results for eligible configurations; core tests assert valid results in normal and strict modes and invalid results without a project.

candidate_atomics.name: construct-client-with-authentication-mode-and-absent-key
candidate_atomics.description: Select the provider-specific SDK mode from the resolved authentication type and preserve key absence so the SDK can perform default credential resolution.

semantic_action.intent: Reach the intended service endpoint and allow the SDK to resolve default credentials instead of switching to an incompatible key mode.
semantic_action.pre_state: Client mode can depend on a preflight environment-variable side effect, while a placeholder or propagated key can select an incompatible authentication mode.
semantic_action.post_state: The selected authentication type deterministically enables the correct SDK mode and no API key is passed for the default-credential path.
semantic_action.validation: The client-construction test clears the mode side effect and verifies GoogleGenAI receives vertexai=true and apiKey=undefined before a token-count request.

candidate_atomics.name: map-missing-credential-errors-to-actionable-alternatives
candidate_atomics.description: Offer the project-based credential alternative only when the current provider configuration can actually use it.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent error guidance from steering users toward placeholder keys or toward a fallback forbidden by their provider entry.
semantic_action.pre_state: Missing-key errors point only to API-key configuration even when a supported keyless path exists, or could misleadingly suggest that path for an entry whose declared key remains mandatory.
semantic_action.post_state: Eligible missing-key errors mention the project-based alternative, while unrelated authentication types and explicit-key entries retain key-specific guidance.
semantic_action.validation: CLI and core tests assert presence of the project hint for eligible missing-key cases and absence for other authentication types and declared-key entries.

candidate_atomics.name: report-routing-configuration-as-indeterminate-authentication
candidate_atomics.description: Represent a project-only preflight state as unknown until session startup resolves the actual default credential.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid reporting a usable token solely because routing configuration exists.
semantic_action.pre_state: Preflight sees no API key for an authentication type with registered key variables and would report a warning, while a project value alone cannot prove that default credentials resolve.
semantic_action.post_state: Preflight reports an indeterminate authentication state with no false token confirmation or missing-key error; definitive credential validation remains deferred to session startup.
semantic_action.validation: The ACP workspacePreflight test verifies unknown cell status, unknown hasToken, and no errorKind for the project-only configuration.

candidate_workflows.name: enable-default-credential-authentication-without-silent-principal-fallback
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve a startup failure caused by API-key-only gates by defining a bounded keyless eligibility contract, applying it consistently, constructing the client in the intended mode without a key, making diagnostics conditional, and keeping preflight claims weaker than actual credential resolution.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow an explicitly selected service mode to authenticate through its supported default credential chain while preserving explicit key contracts and truthful readiness reporting.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A service supports default credentials, but startup gates require an API key; placeholder keys select the wrong SDK authentication mode; and a project identifier alone does not prove that a credential resolves.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Eligible project-only configurations pass all validation gates and construct the correct keyless client, explicit key-variable contracts still fail closed, diagnostics describe only usable alternatives, and preflight defers credential certainty to session startup.
unresolved_or_deferred: Actual availability and validity of Application Default Credentials remain intentionally deferred to SDK/session startup.
